subject.title: fix(agents): reject non-UTF-8 files in edit and apply_patch

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change existing non-UTF-8 edit and patch operations from silent lossy rewrites to a clear rejection that requires an encoding-aware editor?
rationale: The change prevents irreversible data loss but deliberately stops workflows that previously completed, so acceptance of that compatibility boundary requires maintainer intent rather than automated judgment.

options.title: Accept strict rejection
options.body: Treat invalid UTF-8 as unsupported input and merge once the refreshed current-main review confirms all read paths fail before writing.

options.title: Preserve lossy behavior
options.body: Keep existing compatibility for legacy-encoded files, accepting that this leaves the reported silent-byte-corruption behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Accept strict rejection
recommendation.body: Treat invalid UTF-8 as unsupported input and merge once the refreshed current-main review confirms all read paths fail before writing.

likelyOwner.reason: A feature-history pass is required to identify the current-main owner of the agent edit and patch mutation boundary.
